t.1.59.1: Having struck down the sons of Vasiṣṭha together with Mahodaya by the power of his austerities, the greatly radiant Viśvāmitra spoke in the midst of the sages.
t.1.59.2: This descendant of Ikṣvāku, renowned as Triśaṅku, most righteous and generous, has come to me for refuge, desiring to win the world of the gods in this very body of his own.
t.1.59.3: Let the sacrifice be performed by you together with me in such a way that this man will go to the world of the gods in his own body.
t.1.59.4: Having heard the words of Viśvāmitra, all the great sages, knowers of dharma, came together and, united, spoke words in accord with dharma.
t.1.59.5: This sage, the descendant of Kuśika, is exceedingly wrathful; whatever word he has spoken must be carried out properly, there is no doubt.
t.1.59.6: For the blessed one, like fire itself, will pronounce a curse if he is angered; therefore let the sacrifice be set in motion, so that he may go to heaven in his own body.
t.1.59.7: By the power of Viśvāmitra, may the heir of Ikṣvāku go to heaven. Therefore let the sacrifice be set in motion; all of you, take your places and carry it forward.
t.1.59.9: And the officiating priests, skilled in the sacred formulas, performed all the rites in due order, accompanied by mantras, according to the ritual code and in keeping with the prescribed rules.
t.1.59.8: Having spoken thus, the great sages then assembled those rites, and the greatly radiant Viśvāmitra became the officiating priest at the sacrifice.
t.1.59.10: Then, after a long time, Viśvāmitra of great austerity performed there the invocation of all the deities so that they might receive their share of the offerings.
t.1.59.11: Though summoned to receive their shares, all the deities did not come then. Thereupon the great sage Viśvāmitra was filled with anger.
t.1.59.12: Raising the sacrificial ladle in wrath, he said this to Triśaṅku: "Behold the power of my austerity, earned by my own effort, O lord of men!"
t.1.59.13: I myself, by my own power, am leading you to heaven in your own body. Go, O lord of men, in your own body to heaven, which is so hard to attain.
t.1.59.14: For there is indeed some fruit of austerity earned by my own self; O king, by the power of that, go to heaven with your body.
t.1.59.15: When that sage had spoken these words, O Kākutstha, the lord of men rose to heaven in his own body, while the sages looked on.
t.1.59.16: Seeing Triśaṅku arrived in the world of the gods, Pākaśāsana, together with all the hosts of the gods, spoke these words.
t.1.59.18: Thus addressed by the great Indra, Triśaṅku fell down again, crying out "Save me!" to Viśvāmitra, whose wealth was his austerity.
t.1.59.17: Triśaṅku, go back again; you are not one who has earned a dwelling in heaven. Struck down by your guru's curse, you fool, fall to the earth headlong!
t.1.59.19: Hearing those words of him as he cried out, Kauśika was seized by fierce anger and said, "Stay, stay!"
t.1.59.20: In the midst of the sages, that radiant one, like a second Prajāpati, created once more another set of Seven Sages stationed in the southern path.
t.1.59.21: Seized by wrath, the greatly renowned one, taking his stand in the southern quarter amid the sages, created another garland of stars.
t.1.59.22: Clouded with anger, he created a lineage of stars and declared, "I shall make another Indra, or else the world shall be without an Indra!" In his wrath he even began to create gods.
t.1.59.23: Then the foremost of the gods, together with the hosts of sages, greatly alarmed, spoke conciliatory words to the great-souled Viśvāmitra.
t.1.59.24: O greatly fortunate one, O you whose wealth is austerity, this king, struck down by the curse of his guru, is surely not fit to go to heaven in his bodily form.
t.1.59.25: Having heard those words of the gods, Kauśika, the foremost of sages, spoke a most momentous speech to all the deities.
t.1.59.26: Blessings upon you! Having promised the ascent of this king Triśaṅku with his body, I cannot bring myself to make it false.
t.1.59.27: Let this creation of mine for Triśaṅku, here in his bodily form, be everlasting, and let all my stars likewise remain fixed and enduring.
t.1.59.28: As long as the worlds endure, let all these things created by me remain in every way; O gods, all of you ought to grant this.
t.1.59.29: Thus addressed, all the gods replied to the bull among sages.
t.1.59.30: So be it, may good fortune be yours! Let all these many stars remain in the sky, outside the path of Vaiśvānara.
t.1.59.32: But the righteous Viśvāmitra, of great splendor, praised by all the gods and by the sages, said to the deities, "So be it."
t.1.59.31: Let the stars remain, O best of sages, and among those luminaries let Triśaṅku stand, blazing, head turned downward, resembling an immortal.
t.1.59.33: Then, O best of men, at the end of the sacrifice, the great-souled gods and the sages rich in austerity all went back the way they had come.
